headline: Nations Championship: Liam McConnell shines as 11-try Scotland dismantle Japan
author: Tom English

paragraphs.text: Scotland (29) 67
Tries: Graham 3, McConnell 3, Rowe, Smith 2, Dobie, Hutchinson Cons: Jordan 4, Horne 2
Japan (0) 5
Tries: Matsunaga
A Liam McConnell hat-trick in only his third appearance inspired Scotland in an 11-try Nations Championship rout of Japan at Murrayfield.
The 22-year-old Edinburgh back row was electrifying, not just in scoring three wonderful tries, but on both sides of the ball, attack and defence.

The sparkling Darcy Graham also got a hat-trick - his 39th, 40th and 41st international tries - against Eddie Jones' severely weakened team, blasted to kingdom come by England last weekend, and now on the end of another bruising experience.

They shipped five tries in an opening half that ended with the Scots leading 29-0. Game over. Graham got two of his in that opening spell with McConnell getting his first, with Kyle Rowe and Ollie Smith adding the others.

There's been considerable buzz about McConnell for a long time now and significant frustration among his supporters at his lack of opportunities with Scotland. He got his second and third scores before the hour. Jamie Dobie added a seventh.
Gregor Townsend changed most of his team from the win over the Wallabies last Sunday but the second string, if you can call them that, were at it right from the start.

Dobie's box-kick was spilled by the visitors and the last person they would have wanted to seize on the loose ball was Graham. He hacked on and scored. Tom Jordan, playing 10 instead of Finn Russell, was errant off the tee for much of the day and missed the first of his conversions. George Horne came on later and banged over some extras.
Scotland never relented in the building of their points mountain. Kyle Rowe took the ball in the air and the appreciation of space and speed of execution was too much for Japan after that.

Smith, heavily influential at full-back, was at the heart of so many things and he linked with Graham to put McConnell away. The big back row with his giant stride and his fantastic pace ate up the ground to score.

Rowe scored the third after brilliant running from Graham. Barely a quarter of the Test gone and it was already 17-0. Graham's solo score, following a sumptuous pick-up off the floor, brought up the bonus point just after the hour. The wing sped away to score under the posts.

Japan were reeling at the accuracy and the ambition of the Scotland attack. Getting cut open repeatedly, they had no answers. A fifth try arrived just before the break when Japan kicked, rather unwisely and aimlessly, out of defence - just meat and drink to Scotland.
McConnell's outstanding running put the hosts on the front foot and Japan in the horrors. Dobie and Rory Hutchinson set up Smith in the corner.

You felt for Japan. Rabbits in the headlights. McConnell's second came via more thrilling stuff from Darcy who picked up, chipped ahead and gathered to get in behind Japan. He offloaded to the rapid flanker who sprinted in from distance.

A form of Japanese consolation came when full-back Takuro Matsunaga scored but the Scottish response was swift and brutal. McConnell again, of course. He won the ball in the air and flew away to glory. A statement performance albeit against a broken team.
Dobie got the next after nice work from the quietly impressive Hutchinson and Smith got his second and Scotland's ninth after Blair Kinghorn had entered the fray with impact.
The last thing on earth that Japan needed was two yellow cards in the last 10 minutes but that's what they got.
Hutchinson scored not long after it became 15 versus 14 and Graham completed his own hat-trick when it was 15 versus 13.

A savage day for Japan but an unforgettable experience for the hat-trick men - especially the serial-scorer Graham and the emerging star McConnell. His smile at the end was so bright it could have powered half the city's electricity for the night.
